children: In just a few hours from now, the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) will be called a public company, as it will make its stock market debut. The three-day Initial Public Offer (IPO), the biggest of 2026 so far and the second-largest in Indian's capital markets history, received healthy subscription from both institutional and non-institutional investors. Even the retail portion was fully subscribed on the final day of bidding. At ₹4.42 lakh crore market capitalisation, NSE will become the 11th biggest company in India, ahead of Titan, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and even Infosys. What can be called a confidence boost for investors, Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), one of NSE's largest shareholders, bought further stake in the IPO, instead of being a selling shareholder. LIC bought stake worth another ₹450 crore, taking its overall stake to 10.81%. From 3.1 crore unique investors, NSE now boasts of a unique client list of 12.91 crore. What needs to be watched is potential supply from wealth clients, what kind of institutional appetite it garners post listing, and inclusion in foreign indices could also lead to passive inflows. Watch this space for all the LIVE listing updates of NSE.

title: NSE Listing LIVE Updates: Biggest debut of 2026 takes shape in a few hours
